questions.statement: Complete: "I smell the flowers with my ______."
questions.context: En el Festival de las Flores de Medellín, los niños se acercan a oler las orquídeas de las silletas.

options.feedback: Correct. The nose is the part of the face we use to smell things like flowers.
Incorrect. Ears are for hearing sounds, not for smelling flowers.
Incorrect. Eyebrows are the lines of hair above the eyes, and they cannot smell.
Incorrect. Cheeks are the soft sides of the face, and we do not smell with them.

questions.explanation: La palabra "nose" significa nariz, y con la nariz sentimos los olores. Por eso la oración correcta es "I smell the flowers with my nose" (huelo las flores con mi nariz).
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which word names the two lines of hair above your eyes?
questions.context: En una clase de arte en Duitama, los niños dibujan un autorretrato y la profesora nombra cada parte de la cara.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Teeth are white and hard and live inside the mouth, not above the eyes.
Incorrect. Cheeks are under the eyes, on the sides of the nose, and they have no lines of hair.
Incorrect. The mouth is under the nose, and it is for eating and talking.
Correct. Eyebrows are the two lines of hair just above the eyes.

questions.explanation: "Eyebrows" significa cejas. La palabra tiene dentro "eye" (ojo) porque las cejas están justo encima de los ojos. Las mejillas ("cheeks") están debajo y la boca ("mouth") más abajo.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: "Martina sees the rainbow with her ______."
questions.context: Después de la lluvia en Villa de Leyva, Martina mira un arcoíris sobre el cielo.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The mouth is for eating and talking; it cannot see a rainbow.
Incorrect. The nose is for smelling, and seeing a rainbow needs another part of the face.
Correct. We see colors and things like a rainbow with our eyes.
Incorrect. Teeth are for biting and chewing food, not for seeing.

questions.explanation: El verbo "see" significa ver, y vemos con los ojos, que en inglés se dicen "eyes". Por eso "Martina sees the rainbow with her eyes" (Martina ve el arcoíris con sus ojos).
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Read: "After running, Juan's ______ are red. They are on both sides of his nose, under his eyes."
questions.context: Juan corre en el parque Simón Bolívar de Bogotá bajo el sol y su cara se pone roja.

options.feedback: Incorrect. Eyebrows are above the eyes, but the text says the part is under the eyes.
Correct. Cheeks are on both sides of the nose, under the eyes, and they get red when we run.
Incorrect. Ears are on the sides of the head, far from the nose, not under the eyes.
Incorrect. Teeth are inside the mouth, so they are not on the sides of the nose.

questions.explanation: "Cheeks" significa mejillas o cachetes. Están a cada lado de la nariz y debajo de los ojos, justo donde dice el texto. Cuando corremos o hace calor, las mejillas se ponen rojas.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete: "Look at Ana. She ______ big brown eyes."
questions.context: En Riohacha, Samuel describe a su amiga Ana para el juego "¿Quién es quién?" de la clase de inglés.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Have" goes with I, you, we and they; with "She" the verb needs an -s ending.
Incorrect. "Is" describes what a person is, but "She is big brown eyes" says Ana is a pair of eyes.
Incorrect. "Are" goes with you, we and they, and it does not express that Ana owns her eyes.
Correct. With "She" we use "has" to say what a person's face is like: "She has big brown eyes".

questions.explanation: Para describir la cara usamos el verbo "have" (tener). Con "I" y "you" se dice "have", pero con "He" o "She" cambia a "has". Por eso decimos "She has big brown eyes" (ella tiene ojos grandes y cafés).
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "My name is Andres. I have short black hair and green eyes. I have a small nose and a big smile."
What color are Andres's eyes?
questions.context: Andres, un niño de Quibdó, escribe una descripción de su cara para su amigo por correspondencia.

options.feedback: Incorrect. In the text "black" describes his hair, not his eyes.
Correct. The text says "green eyes", so the eyes of Andres are green.
Incorrect. The word "brown" does not appear in the text about Andres.
Incorrect. The text never says "blue"; the color next to "eyes" is green.

questions.explanation: En inglés el color va antes de la palabra que describe: "black hair" es cabello negro y "green eyes" es ojos verdes. Hay que fijarse qué palabra acompaña a "eyes": es "green", entonces los ojos de Andres son verdes.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Read: "Luisa has long curly hair and brown eyes. She has a small mouth and she wears glasses."
Which sentence is true?
questions.context: En Montería, Gabriel describe a su prima Luisa, que tiene el cabello rizado y usa gafas.

options.feedback: Incorrect. The text says "long curly hair", and long is the opposite of short.
Incorrect. The text says her eyes are brown, not blue.
Correct. The text says "She has a small mouth", so this sentence matches the description.
Incorrect. The text describes her mouth as "small", and big is the opposite.

questions.explanation: Para evaluar cada oración hay que compararla con el texto. Luisa tiene cabello largo ("long"), ojos cafés ("brown") y boca pequeña ("small mouth"). Solo la oración "Luisa has a small mouth" coincide con la descripción.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.context: En Yopal, la profesora muestra cuatro descripciones de caras para un mural y pide encontrar la que está bien escrita.

options.text: He has a small nose and two big eyes.
options.feedback: Correct. "He" goes with "has", and "two eyes" uses the plural because there are two of them.
Incorrect. With "one" we need the singular "eye"; "eyes" is the plural for two or more.
Incorrect. With "She" the verb must be "has", so "She have" is a grammar mistake.
Incorrect. With "I" we use "have", because "has" only goes with he, she and it.

questions.explanation: Para describir la cara recordamos dos reglas: "I have" pero "He/She has", y una sola cosa va en singular ("one eye", "one nose") mientras dos o más van en plural ("two eyes", "two ears"). Solo la opción A cumple las dos reglas.
questions.subject: ingles
